source.title: Simply B1 Preliminary for Schools: 8 Complete Practice Tests (2019, revised exam from 2020)
source.answerKeyOrigin: Prepared for WordHop from the supplied reading text; not a publisher-provided answer key.
source.explanationOrigin: Written for WordHop with evidence from the supplied text.

questions.explanation: Sue is asked to buy more vegetables because guests are coming for dinner. Her mother says she will be a little late, not that she will miss dinner completely.
questions.evidence: get some extra vegetables for dinner

questions.explanation: A deposit is money paid beforehand. The notice refers to the students' £10 locker deposit, from which the cost of replacing lost keys is taken.
questions.evidence: your £10.00 member locker users deposit

questions.explanation: The bicycle-parking ban on weekdays ends at 6 pm, so late Friday-night parking is permitted. At weekends, the road is only for pedestrians.
questions.evidence: Bicycle Parking not permitted Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm

questions.explanation: The forecast predicts frequent showers, so Tony expects wet weather. He suggests comfortable accommodation rather than promising to camp.
questions.evidence: the weather forecast predicts frequent showers

questions.explanation: 'From £5' gives the lowest starting price for shoes. The T-shirt offer requires buying two first, and the notice does not say every item is half price.
questions.evidence: end-of-season shoes, from an incredible £5 a pair

questions.explanation: The Emperors combines an exciting story about historical rulers with illustrations and information about architecture. It matches all of Jake's interests.
questions.evidence: beautifully illustrated with interesting information about the architecture and culture

questions.explanation: Tasty treats offers simple, quick recipes with everyday ingredients. It is suitable for Julia's mother because she has little free time.
questions.evidence: Basic simple food, quick to prepare and at a low cost.

questions.explanation: The Return is a crime mystery whose solution is delayed until the third book. Paul wants a long, gripping mystery that keeps him guessing.
questions.evidence: you won't find out who did it until the third book

questions.explanation: The Search lets readers explore wildlife and beautiful places through photography without leaving home. It matches the grandfather's former work and travel interests.
questions.evidence: full of wonderful photography and interesting facts

questions.explanation: Going to Extremes is a guide to exciting travel destinations and extreme sports. It suits Sharon and Tom's plans for adventurous travel after school.
questions.evidence: the best places for those who love excitement and want to achieve their dream

questions.explanation: Tina says she has decided to become a vet, which is a doctor for animals. She is describing her intended career, not an existing paid job.
questions.evidence: I have already decided that I want to be a vet.

questions.explanation: Tina says she had an amazing time and made many new friends. The trip was volunteering, not a required part of professional training.
questions.evidence: how amazing it would really be or how many new friends I would make

questions.explanation: Tina explains the fishermen's motive: turtles eat fish from their nets, reducing their income. This shows she understands the reason for their actions, without saying those actions are right.
questions.evidence: For the fishermen, however, this has a cost, as fewer fish mean less money.

questions.explanation: Although the campsite had practical difficulties and biting insects, Tina still enjoyed working with turtles and sharing evenings with the volunteers.
questions.evidence: But even that could not stop me from enjoying the daily contact with the turtles.

questions.explanation: Tina is a young volunteer who hopes to become a vet. This description connects her present experience with her future plan to help animals through her career.
questions.evidence: At the age of 14 I have already decided that I want to be a vet.

questions.explanation: H explains what taking cycling 'to a whole new level' involved: a mountain bike and cycling in all weather. The following 'idea' refers back to this commitment.
questions.evidence: I took it to a whole new level.

questions.explanation: G introduces the preference for challenges, which the following list of hills, mountains, forests and difficult landscapes illustrates.
questions.evidence: some of the most difficult landscapes on a bike

questions.explanation: A develops the idea of enjoying the natural environment. The next sentence gives further benefits of being outside away from the city.
questions.evidence: And of course, there's being in the natural environment.

questions.explanation: The previous sentence says the writer was more than merely keen. F explains this stronger reaction: the cycling trip was a dream opportunity.
questions.evidence: I was not just keen.

questions.explanation: C clarifies how narrow and rough the road is. The following sentence supports this by saying it has room for only one vehicle.
questions.evidence: With only space for one vehicle the 1,000 metre drops are terrifying.

questions.explanation: 'Find out' means discover or learn information. The writer enjoyed learning facts about Japanese macaques during the project.
questions.evidence: It was exciting to (21) ... out so much about them.

questions.explanation: 'Ability to' describes being able to do something. The unusual feature is that the monkeys can pass new ideas to other monkeys.
questions.evidence: their (22) ... to pass on new ideas to each other

questions.explanation: A scientific study discovers a behaviour that already exists. It does not invent or design the monkeys' actions.
questions.evidence: something (23) ... in a scientific study

questions.explanation: 'Interested in' is the correct adjective-preposition combination for people who want to learn about macaques.
questions.evidence: People who are (24) ... in the Macaques

questions.explanation: 'Behaviour' describes the way animals act. The paragraph explains how hot bathing became one of their activities through copying.
questions.evidence: this is not part of their typical (25) ...

questions.explanation: 'Freezing cold' is a common expression meaning extremely cold. It naturally describes the day on which the monkey entered the hot water.
questions.evidence: on a(n) (26) ... cold day

questions.explanation: 'Never achieved before' refers to something that has not previously been done. The paragraph introduces a record-breaking achievement.
questions.evidence: things never achieved (27) ...

questions.explanation: Use 'enough' after an adjective: 'brave enough to try'. It means having sufficient courage for the action.
questions.evidence: brave (28) ... to try to do the incredible

questions.explanation: The journey received the action of being recorded. Singular 'journey' therefore needs 'was' to form the past passive with 'recorded'.
questions.evidence: His amazing journey of 157 days (29) ... even recorded in a weekly internet series.

questions.explanation: A modal verb such as 'may' is followed by the base form. 'May be best-known' describes the achievement people know him for most.
questions.evidence: Although he may (30) ... best-known for this achievement

questions.explanation: The structure 'ranging from ... to ...' gives the two ends of a range of examples.
questions.evidence: ranging from running a marathon ... (31) ... completing an Olympic Distance Triathlon

questions.explanation: 'Not so much ... but ...' contrasts the less important reason with the real reason for admiration: the lesson Ross teaches about human ability.
questions.evidence: (32) ... so much that he is one of the fittest men alive, but for the fact that he wishes to teach us
